description:
Payload for ``message_type='registered'``.

The coordinator's answer to ``register``. Registration can legitimately
be refused — an agent may not be approved, or may declare a capability
it is not permitted to offer — and without this answer the agent has no
way to tell refusal from success, so it would keep serving nothing while
believing it was live.

reason.description: Why registration was refused. Empty when accepted.
reason.title: Reason

registered_capabilities.description: Capability IDs the coordinator actually accepted.
registered_capabilities.title: Registered Capabilities

granted_scopes.description: Scopes this agent was actually granted, which is not what it asked for. A scope is granted by a binding an administrator authored (RFC 0003), never by an agent having declared it, so an agent MUST NOT assume its request was honoured.
granted_scopes.title: Granted Scopes

unrecognised_scopes.description: Declared scopes this coordinator's catalogue does not contain. Recorded as a request for an administrator rather than granted.
unrecognised_scopes.title: Unrecognised Scopes

catalogue.description: Scope names this coordinator recognises, returned when a declaration named something outside it. The refusal is how the vocabulary propagates: an implementer learns the right name by being corrected, instead of from documentation that goes stale.
catalogue.title: Catalogue

coordinator_protocol_version.description: The LIP version the coordinator implements, so an agent can detect a mismatch rather than inferring it from failures.
coordinator_protocol_version.title: Coordinator Protocol Version

title: LIP registered payload
